sentences.english_text: The yelling from the crowd was so loud that Drippy could hear what they were saying.
He looked around to see where the saint's tier was and he suddenly realized that it was him.
I'm the miracle.
God sent me here to take care of these people.
Drippy could not get over how important he was.
All these people down in the square below were cheering him.
I always knew I was important and this proves it.
He started to wave to the crowd below.
But he almost lost his balance and he grabbed onto the statue with both hands.
He did not want to fall down into the statue again.
It's a good thing that I didn't listen to the wind.
Why, if I had kept my promise I would still be sitting on that park bench.
None of these people would know that I was a miracle.
And they wouldn't be cheering me.
It just goes to prove that you should never keep your promises.
How wrong Drippy was.
Someone in the crowd said to the priest, What are we going to do now?
That was a good question.
And the priest had to think for a long time before he came up with an answer.
We must preserve the miracle.
We must save the statue's tier.
How do we do that?
Someone will have to go up and bring it down.
When Drippy heard that he was thrilled.
He would not have to find a way down.
They were going to come up and get him.
Of course they were.
Was he not a miracle?
What a story he would have to tell when he got home.
He would tell everybody about how the whole town had got down on their knees and prayed to him.
Down below the priest was talking to a young man.
Get a ladder.
We have to bring the saint's tier down.
And the young man rushed off to get a ladder.
What are you going to do with the tier?
Send it to the Vatican in Rome.
I'm going to Rome.
How exciting.
He was not sure what the Vatican was.
But it sounded interesting.
The Pope knows how to handle miracles, the priest told the crowd.
When word gets out about what happened here today, this will be the most famous town in the world.
Everyone will want to come and pray to the statue of the saint.
He means to pray to me, Drippy thought.
The statue isn't a miracle.
I am.
We'll build a shrine here.
It will be the biggest shrine in the world.
A man in the crowd who owned a restaurant said, With hundreds of thousands of people coming here, they'll need a place to eat.
I'm going to make my restaurant bigger.
And a man who owned a hotel said, All those people coming here to worship will need a place to sleep.
I'm going to build more rooms on my hotel.
And the owner of a bus company said, They'll need buses to go from the railroad station to the park.
I'm going to buy some more buses right away.
And soon everyone who had any kind of business at all was talking about making his business larger to take care of the huge crowds that would be coming to the city where the miracle took place.
And they all thought how rich they were going to be.
Drippy, listen to all of this.
This is going to be the greatest town in the world.
And all because of me.
I wouldn't be surprised if they put up a statue to me.
They can call it the statue of a brave, beautiful, smart raindrop.
And he was very pleased with the idea.
